data.stem: The Battle of Plassey in 1757 marks the beginning of which phase?
data.explanation: East India Company rule is correct because Plassey opened Company dominance. Crown rule is wrong because it began in 1858, while independence and princely rules are wrong because they belong to different phases.
data.label: practice

data.stem: The grant of Diwani in 1765 gave the Company which role in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa?
data.explanation: Revenue administration is correct as the Diwani grant concerned revenue. Crown fleet command is wrong because it confuses naval with fiscal power, while Congress control and presidency ownership are wrong because they belong to later institutions.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Government of India was transferred from the Company to the Crown by which Act in 1858?
data.explanation: Government of India Act, 1858 is correct as the transfer instrument. The 1861, 1935 and 1947 options are wrong because they belong to later constitutional phases.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Crown rule in India continued from 1858 until which year?
data.explanation: 1947 is correct as the independence endpoint. The years 1857 and 1935 are wrong because they are earlier milestones, while 1765 is wrong because it marks Diwani under Company rule.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Jayi Rajaguru and the Paiks of Odisha revolted against the British East India Company in which year?
data.explanation: 1804 is correct as the revolt year in the Company phase. The years 1757, 1858 and 1947 are wrong because they belong to Plassey, Crown takeover and independence respectively.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Jayi Rajaguru was executed at Midnapore on which date?
data.explanation: 6 December 1806 at Midnapore is correct as the execution follows the 1804 revolt. The 1804 date is wrong because it is the revolt year, while 1858 and 1947 are wrong because they belong to Crown takeover and independence.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which sequence correctly orders Company and Crown milestones?
data.explanation: Plassey, Diwani, 1858, 1947 is correct in order. The other sequences are wrong because they place 1858 before 1757, place 1947 first, or swap Plassey and Diwani.
data.label: practice

data.stem: British rule began in 1858. Why is this statement incorrect?
options: Because Company rule began earlier in 1757 and 1765
data.explanation: Company rule began earlier in 1757 and 1765 is correct. British rule in 1947 is wrong because that is the endpoint, while never ruling and Crown in 1757 are wrong because they deny or reverse the Company phase.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Annexation debates including lapse belong to which period?
options: Before the Crown takeover, including the Company phase
data.explanation: Before the Crown takeover is correct because lapse predates 1858. Only after 1858 is wrong because it confines annexation to Crown rule, while after 1947 and twentieth-century-only options are wrong because they place colonial expansion after independence.
data.label: practice

data.stem: The 1804 Rajaguru revolt was directed against whom?
data.explanation: The British East India Company is correct because 1804 falls in the Company phase. The British Crown directly is wrong because the Crown took over in 1858, while Congress and princely states are wrong because they are not the opponent in this revolt.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Jayi Rajaguru is described in the OPSC material as royal preceptor to whom?
data.explanation: Mukundadeva II is correct as the preceptor role in the material. Mughal Emperor, British Governor-General and Peshwa leader are wrong because they misstate the Odisha royal connection.
data.label: practice

data.stem: How were the Odia-speaking areas administered after the British conquest of 1803?
options: All of them under the Bengal Presidency
All of them under the Bombay Presidency
Split: the coastal division under Bengal, southern tracts such as Ganjam under Madras, and Sambalpur later under the Central Provinces
As a separate Odisha province from 1803
data.explanation: The three-way split is correct: Cuttack, Puri and Balasore went with Bengal, Ganjam lay in the Madras Presidency, and Sambalpur was later attached to the Central Provinces. 'All under Bengal' ignores the southern and western tracts, Bombay never governed Odisha, and a separate Odisha province came only on 1 April 1936.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Consider the statements: 1. Company rule preceded Crown rule. 2. Crown rule began in 1757. Which is correct?
data.explanation: 1 only is correct because Company rule came first. The option with 2 only and both are wrong because Crown rule began in 1858 not 1757, while neither is wrong because the first statement is correct.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which pair correctly separates the two phases by agent?
options: Company rule under the Crown; Crown rule under the Company
Company rule under the Company; Crown rule under the sovereign
data.explanation: Company under the Company and Crown under the sovereign is correct. The reversed option is wrong because it swaps the agents, while Congress and princely options are wrong because they misstate colonial agency.
data.label: practice

data.stem: A question pairs each year with its correct event. Which pairing is correct?
data.explanation: Revolt 1804 with Crown takeover 1858 and Diwani 1765 is correct. The other pairings are wrong because they swap revolt and takeover years, assign 1947 to Diwani, or place Plassey in 1858, whereas the correct set keeps each year with its event.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Why does the 1804 revolt also test phase awareness?
options: Because 1804 was against the Crown in 1858
Because 1804 falls in the Company phase before Crown rule
data.explanation: Company phase before Crown rule is correct because 1804 precedes 1858. After independence and Crown in 1858 options are wrong because they place 1804 after 1947 or in the Crown phase, while 1947 transfer option repeats the same error.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which statement best advises a learner on lapse questions?
options: Confine lapse only to post-1858 history
Treat lapse as beginning with independence
Ignore lapse because it is not in the syllabus
Place lapse and annexation before the Crown takeover
data.explanation: Placing lapse before the takeover is correct as the examination guidance. Confining lapse to post-1858 is wrong because annexation predates 1858, while independence and ignore-lapse options are wrong because they remove a syllabus topic.
data.label: practice

data.stem: An option says Rajaguru was executed before the revolt. Why is it incorrect?
options: Because the revolt was in 1858 and execution in 1947
Because execution preceded revolt in the same year
Because the revolt was in 1804 and execution in 1806
data.explanation: Revolt in 1804 and execution in 1806 is correct because execution follows the revolt. The 1858 and 1947 years are wrong because they belong to Crown rule and independence, while same-year precedence and denial of the revolt are wrong because they contradict the 1804 to 1806 sequence.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which conclusion about colonial rule is most defensible from the cited material?
options: Company and Crown rule were identical in agency
British rule began with the Crown in 1757
Company rule 1757 and 1765 to 1858 was followed by Crown rule to 1947
data.explanation: Company to 1858 followed by Crown to 1947 is correct as the two-phase conclusion. Identical agency is wrong because the agent changed, 1757 Crown is wrong because it reverses the phases, and Odisha after 1858 only is wrong because the 1804 revolt predates 1858.
data.label: practice

data.stem: A timeline item reads: Plassey followed Diwani, and the revolt followed Crown rule. What is wrong with it?
options: The revolt followed Crown rule is correct
Plassey preceded Diwani and the revolt preceded Crown rule
data.explanation: Precedence of Plassey and revolt is correct because 1757 precedes 1765 and 1804 precedes 1858. Each single correct claim is wrong because the timeline reverses both orders, while both correct is wrong because both orders are reversed.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Consider the following statements about Jayi Rajaguru: 1. He was royal preceptor to Mukundadeva II. 2. He mobilised the Paiks against the East India Company in 1804. 3. He was executed at Cuttack in 1817. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
data.explanation: 1 and 2 only is correct: Rajaguru was preceptor to Mukundadeva II and led the Paiks against the Company in 1804. Statement 3 is wrong because he was executed at Midnapore on 6 December 1806, so any option containing 3 is wrong, and '1 only' leaves out the true statement 2.
data.label: pyq-pattern
